name: Electrum Ravencoin 1.2.4
body:
Changes:
- Added support for more Trezor models
- Allow the use of the BTC app on ledger models
- Removed BTC addresses in certain help messages and replaced them with RVN equivalents

Migrating from versions earlier than v1.0.0? Read the release notes for [that version](https://github.com/Electrum-RVN-SIG/electrum-ravencoin/releases/tag/v1.0.1).

body:

name: Electrum Ravencoin 1.2.2
body:
Bug Fixes:
- Prevent crash if a IPFS lookup from inside of an asset lookup fails

Changes:
- Updates public IPFS explorers
- Optimizations for local IPFS gateways

Migrating from versions earlier than v1.0.0? Read the release notes for [that version](https://github.com/Electrum-RVN-SIG/electrum-ravencoin/releases/tag/v1.0.1).

name: Electrum Ravencoin 1.2.1
body:
Due to the nature of this bug fix, I wanted to release some kind of binary as soon as possible. This version only contains binaries for Windows and Linux. MacOS binaries will be built for the next version as more work is needed due to recent Apple changes.

Bug Fixes:
- Persistent crash on chain forks in some cases has been fixed

New Features:
- Visually indicate when a new broadcast is available
- Update IPFS data type identification logic and default IPFS explorers

Migrating from versions earlier than v1.0.0? Read the release notes for [that version](https://github.com/Electrum-RVN-SIG/electrum-ravencoin/releases/tag/v1.0.1).

name: Electrum Ravencoin 1.2.0
body:
New Features:
- When displaying IPFS data in-app, data is downloaded as a CAR block and then decoded to verify that the data is actually that of the IPFS hash.

Migrating from versions earlier than v1.0.0? Read the release notes for [that version](https://github.com/Electrum-RVN-SIG/electrum-ravencoin/releases/tag/v1.0.1).

name: Electrum Ravencoin 1.1.0
body:
New Features:
- View IPFS hashes as base32 CIDv1
- Ability to view asset metadata histories
- More IPFS caching options

Bug Fixes:
- Fix some versions of windows computers not being able to open the executables
- Don't show fiat values on assets
- Validate an asset was entered in the watch broadcasts text box

name: Electrum Ravencoin 1.0.1
body:
The big 1.0 Release!
This is a complete re-write from https://github.com/spesmilo/electrum/commit/b5654b640a51a37de96f897da545b7bb39c68003

- Mainnet multisig, atomic swaps, broadcasts, and restricted asset operations are now built-in

- Better IPFS lookups and support for local ipfs nodes

- Developer notifications are broadcast on `ELECTRUM_RAVENCOIN~notification` and will be automatically subscribed to

- All following updates will be signed with PGP instead of the in-wallet signature verification. My key can be found at [/pubkeys](https://github.com/Electrum-RVN-SIG/electrum-ravencoin/tree/master/pubkeys) as well as the first broadcast on `ELECTRUM_RAVENCOIN~notification`

- v1.0.1: Fixed compilation error where bip39 word lists were not included in windows and mac binaries

IMPORTANT: Due to the re-write, unfortunately wallets will need to be re-created. Contacts and labels can be exported and re-imported without issue. 
Hardware wallets:
- Follow the same steps as when you created your wallet; the addresses will all be the same

Software wallets:
- If you do not know your seed, it can be found by clicking the "sprouting seed" icon in the bottom right of your current version.
- When opening version 1.0.x, create a new wallet then select Standard Wallet > I already have a seed, then input your seed. (Click options if you have a mnemonic passphrase in which case you should choose "Extend this seed with custom words")

name: Electrum Ravencoin 0.4.0
body:
Looking for pre-built binaries? Click “assets” below this text box.

**UPDATE**
Some users are reporting that the number of headers is not increasing in the lower right hand corner when doing an initial wallet sync. The headers are still being downloaded and verified; this is purely a visual bug. This process should take around half an hour to complete before any transactions you might have will be visible. Expect a release in the coming week fixing this and adding some more UI information about syncing headers.

This update allows for the creation and reissuance of main, sub, and unique assets as well as the transference of assets. (These asset features are not available yet for hardware wallets (for new electrum users, sending RVN is perfectly fine on hardware). If this becomes available before the next update, I expect I will use the new messages tab rather than push an official update.)

I have also introduced BIP39 into electrum to allow for better inter-wallet usages. Users may choose one of several BIP39 languages or the default electrum seed. Users may also import any non-extended core or mobile wallet BIP39 phrase into electrum.

Look forward to in the next update:

    RIP 10 compliance (asset metadata encoding scheme)
    Integrated atomic swaps
    Asset messages and broadcasts
    The ability to view asset IPFS data in-wallet
    More BIP39 seed phrase options

In addition, from now on, I will posting the SHA256 check-sums of the pre-built binaries signed by my address to ensure its validity. When you are notified of updates in the future, you will have the option to verify these check-sums in the update window. The signing address to verify against is hard-coded in electrum ravencoin.

name: Electrum Ravencoin 0.3.0
body:
*UPDATE AGAIN* Sorry everyone, I sorely underestimated the amount of an average user's transactions. Updated the default max receive amount to 10MB.

*UPDATE* Increased client side max receive amount to 2MB.

Looking for pre-built binaries? Click “assets” below this text box.

This update allows users to receive, but not send assets. The next update will allow for asset receiving and sending functionality.

If you previously used electrum ravencoin, there are some file architecture overhauls. You may either re-enter your seed phrase when starting up electrum or copy (make sure to copy just in case) your wallet file from the old electrum ravencoin location ($HOME/.electrum-raven or electrum_data) to the new one ($HOME/.electrum-raven, electrum_ravencoin_data, or %appdata%\roaming\Electrum-Ravencoin).

While I figure out how to sign binaries, the prebuilt apps will give warnings when you download them. If you don't trust this, see how to build your own binaries here:
https://github.com/Electrum-RVN-SIG/electrum-ravencoin/blob/master/README.rst

You will also need to resync the electrum chain. If for whatever reason you would like to skip this, see here:
https://github.com/Electrum-RVN-SIG/prebuilts/tree/master/blockchain_header_files
